title: fix(i18n): recognise a spec translation bundle by any group it carries
body:
Fixes #10235

## What was wrong

`apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts` asks `isSpecTranslationData` (from `@object-ui/i18n`) whether the payload it fetched is a spec `TranslationData`. On `true` the payload goes through `transformSpecTranslations` and lands under the `app` namespace, where `useObjectLabel` and the screen-flow runner read it. On `false` it is returned untouched. That branch exists for a mock or local-dev server that already serves i18next namespaces. The predicate answered `true` only when some `objects` entry carried `fields`. A genuine bundle that translated object labels, apps, pages, dashboards or flows, but no field label, therefore sat at the root of the resource tree, and nothing read it.

## What changed

- `packages/i18n/src/utils/spec-translations.ts`: `isSpecTranslationData` now recognises a payload by any top-level group of the served translation document, provided that group's value is a plain object. The eleven groups are written out in a module-private `SPEC_TRANSLATION_GROUPS`. `@object-ui/i18n` deliberately does not depend on `@objectstack/spec`, so the list cannot be imported there. The pin against the spec lives beside the console loader (see below).
- `apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts` is **unchanged**. Its branch was right, but its recogniser was wrong.
- `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/spec-translations.test.ts`: the old test pinned the defect (label-only bundle answered `false`). It is replaced by these tests:
  - a label-only bundle is recognised;
  - the groups the card names are each recognised alone;
  - four flat controls stay on the as-is branch:
    - an app namespace (`crm`), a built-in namespace (`common`), and the envelope-less error body the e2e boot mock serves;
    - the transform's own output, so nothing is wrapped twice;
    - a group-named key holding a string, an array or null;
    - every built-in locale pack namespace, read off `builtInLocales` at run time. None of them is spelled like a spec group.
  - Two transform pins cover the label-only and flows-only shapes.
- `apps/console/src/loadLanguage.test.tsx` (new, beside the loader; the console depends on the spec):
  - walks `GetTranslationsResponseSchema.shape.translations` key by key. For each group it requires that a payload carrying that group alone is spec-valid (`safeParse` succeeds) and that the real loader answers with exactly the `app` namespace;
  - puts an object-label-only bundle through the real loader, then renders `useObjectLabel().objectLabel` and gets `线索`, not `Lead` (the card's probe);
  - puts a flows-only bundle through the real loader, then renders `FlowRunner`, which draws the translated heading and field label;
  - returns an app-namespaced tree and an envelope-less built-in override byte-for-byte as-is.
- `.changeset/10235-spec-translation-bundle-recognised-by-any-group.md`: `@object-ui/i18n` patch.

## Premise and mechanism assumptions, measured

- **Premise holds** on `origin/main` `1dbb9933c`: the predicate required an `objects` entry with `fields`, and the loader returned a `false` answer untransformed.
- **A1: where the group list comes from.** `@objectstack/spec` exports no key-list constant for the translation groups. I read the list off the schema's shape at run time instead.
  - Installed spec 17.4.0: `GetTranslationsResponseSchema.shape.translations` and `TranslationDataSchema` have the same eleven keys: `objects`, `apps`, `messages`, `globalActions`, `dashboards`, `datasets`, `pages`, `flows`, `settings`, `metadataForms`, `settingsCommon`.
  - objectstack `main` (`61609ed`): the per-app `TranslationDataSchema` drops `settings`. The served document is typed as `PlatformTranslationDataSchema` (the per-app groups plus `settings`), and that has the same eleven. So the pin reads the response schema, not the per-app one. That choice keeps it correct across the split.
  - Two i18n tests record the precedent that `@object-ui/i18n` must not depend on the spec, including test-only (`dashboard-range-preset-labels-4984.test.ts`, `marketplace-preview-namespace-3546.test.tsx`). That is why the list is hand-written.
  - ⚠️ **The pin catches drift in one direction only.** A group the spec adds and the list lacks turns it red (ablation 2 below). A group the list keeps after the spec drops it is not detected: the list is module-private, and exporting it would widen `@object-ui/i18n`'s public index outside the claimed file surface.
- **A2: what a flat payload looks like here.** No MSW or mock translation server remains in objectui. The endpoint's only callers are:
  - the console loader;
  - `examples/console-starter`'s loader;
  - the e2e boot mock, which answers `{ success: true, data: {} }`.

  Test loaders feed namespaced trees such as `{ common: { save } }`. None of these has a top-level spec-group key. The rule needs the key **and** a plain-object value, and the tests read the built-in pack namespaces at run time to check that none collides with a group.
  - One shape changes branch: an un-namespaced, already-flattened tree carrying a top-level `objects` key (the shape the old doc comment named). It now goes through the transform. No producer of it exists in either repo.
  - Before the fix, that shape was unreadable at the root anyway: `getAppNamespaces` looks for `objects` and similar keys one level down, inside a namespace. The transform now wraps it under `app`, forwarding its `fields` and `fieldOptions` verbatim.
- **A3: the transform on these shapes.** A label-only payload and a flows-only payload go through the real transform without throwing. They come out exactly as `{ app: { objects: … } }` and `{ app: { flows } }` (pinned in the i18n test, and exercised end to end through the loader in the console test).

## Evidence (every run at `bb6682c51`)

- **Tests.** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/i18n/ apps/console/src/loadLanguage.test.tsx packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/FlowRunner.flowsTranslation-5920.test.tsx packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.defaultViewIdentity.test.tsx`: `Test Files 73 passed (73)`, `Tests 1180 passed (1180)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The two app-shell files are the other callers of `isSpecTranslationData`.
- **Ablations** (all three through `ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty):
  1. The predicate body reverted to the old `objects.NAME.fields` rule: **5 red / 15 green**. The five are:
     - the label-only pin;
     - the any-group pin;
     - the spec-key walk (`objects: expected [ 'objects' ] to deeply equal [ 'app' ]`);
     - the label render (`Unable to find … heading … "线索"`);
     - the wizard render (`… "转化详情"`).

     The flat controls stay green in both directions, as predicted: they pin the unchanged branch.
  2. `'datasets'` deleted from the list: **1 red**, the spec-key walk (`datasets: expected [ 'datasets' ] to deeply equal [ 'app' ]`).
  3. The value-shape check replaced by `!== undefined`: **2 red**, the existing `{ objects: null }` / `{ objects: [] }` pin and the new group-named non-object pin.
- **Type checks.**
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n run type-check` passes, after building the dependency closure (`--filter '@object-ui/i18n^...'`, then i18n itself). `--listFiles` on `tsconfig.test.json` shows it compiles `spec-translations.test.ts`.
  - The console's own `type-check` resolves `@object-ui/*` through built `dist/` for the whole dependency closure. That run is ⚠️ **NOT MEASURED**, reason: it needs the console's full build closure, and CI's Type Check job runs it.
  - Measured instead: a temporary tsconfig extending the console's own, with `@object-ui/*` mapped to package sources and the new test file as a root. It reported 93 errors, all in other packages' sources under the console's stricter options, and **0 in `loadLanguage.test.tsx`**.
- **Gates**, all exit 0:
  - `check-changeset-presence` (3 source files of 2 released packages, 1 changeset declared);
  - `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`;
  - `check-changeset-claims` (report-only, nothing to re-read);
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`;
  - `check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`);
  - `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`.
- **Lint, narrowed to the touched files.**
  - Scope: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the three touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files. They match the config's `**/*.{ts,tsx}` block, and the JSON reports 3 files, 0 errors, 5 warnings.
  - The 5 warnings are the pre-existing `no-explicit-any` casts in the transform tests. The same file at `1dbb9933c` reports the same 5.
  - Why the narrowing holds: `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/FlowRunner.flowsTranslation-5920.test.tsx` says its fixture carries `objects` "because `isSpecTranslationData` keys off it". That is no longer true. The test stays green, since its fixture still carries a field label. Comment only; outside this claim's file surface.
- `SpecTranslationData` and `PASSTHROUGH_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` in `spec-translations.ts` name `validationMessages`. No spec version read here declares it, and the spec shape is strict, so an author writing it is refused at publish. The transform forwarding it is harmless. Not filed: no named producer.
- The `transformSpecTranslations` doc says `getAppNamespaces` "keys off the presence of `objects` and `fields`". It also keys off `apps`, `dashboards`, `pages`, `reports` and `globalActions`. Comment drift; left alone.
- Readers of the groups that now reach `app` alone: `useObjectLabel` reads only groups its discovery lists; `FlowRunner` and the console's `useSettingsLabel` discover namespaces by their own group (`flows`, `settings` / `settingsCommon`). So a flows-only or settings-only bundle is read once it is namespaced.
- Out of scope, reported to the seat rather than filed here: `examples/console-starter`'s loader returns the spec payload with no transform at all. A probe against the built i18n dist renders `Lead` for a bundle that even carries a field label. The same bundle through `transformSpecTranslations` renders `线索`.
